extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities, child welfare advocates, immigration attorneys, state agencies, and public commenters on the NPRM
extracted.subtask_short: ORR UC care NPRM comment drafting
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply the proposed regulatory standards and definitions governing the placement, care, and services for unaccompanied children in ORR custody to inform comments, compliance, or implementation. Focuses on ORR's NPRM (proposed part 410) to codify FSA provisions and statutory duties under the HSA and TVPRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: TVPRA notification and transfer timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must notify HHS within 48 hours of apprehending or discovering an unaccompanied child or receiving a claim/suspicion that a non-citizen is an unaccompanied child; absent exceptional circumstances, transfer custody to HHS within 72 hours of determining the child is unaccompanied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures ORR custody and that HHS establishes protections against traffickers and other exploiters; the NPRM reiterates these statutory timelines as foundational to ORR responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSA: least restrictive setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Minors must be placed in the 'least restrictive setting appropriate to the minor's age and special needs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a primary substantive requirement from the Flores Settlement Agreement that ORR intends to implement and codify where applicable for ORR custody decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSA: release priority for sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: When release is appropriate, priority for potential sponsors is: a parent, legal guardian, adult relative, or another adult designated by the parent or legal guardian as capable and willing to care for the minor's well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no sponsor is available, placement at a care provider facility licensed by an appropriate state agency is required; the NPRM codifies this order of preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSA: bond hearing entitlement and opt-out
rubrics_metrics.description: Any non‑citizen child who remains in government custody for removal proceedings is entitled to a bond hearing before an immigration judge, unless the minor indicates on the Notice of Custody Determination form that he or she refuses such a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM references this FSA provision and the Ninth Circuit's interpretation (see discussion of hearing process consistency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit 1 minimum standards for licensed care provider facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Flores Settlement Agreement's Exhibit 1 describes minimum standards required at licensed care provider facilities caring for unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM intends to implement the protections set forth in the FSA and to codify minimum facility standards (and to ensure programs meet Exhibit 1-equivalent minimums even where state licensure is unavailable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to codify and publish FSA terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The FSA states that within 120 days of final district court approval, the Government shall initiate action to publish the relevant and substantive terms of the Agreement in regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical procedural requirement motivating prior and current rulemakings; NPRM references this as background for regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR authority to coordinate care and placement (§410.1002)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR has authority to coordinate and implement the care and placement of unaccompanied children in ORR custody by reason of their immigration status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies ORR's scope of authority aligned with prior rules (45 CFR 410.102(a)) and statutory duties under HSA and TVPRA; the NPRM asserts ORR's jurisdiction for part 410.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of part provisions (§410.1000(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed provisions of part 410 are separate and severable; if a provision is stayed or invalidated, remaining provisions shall continue in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR signals intent for operational continuity even if courts invalidate particular provisions; ORR may later amend provisions if required by judicial holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: part does not govern entire UC program (§410.1000(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed part 410 pertains to placement, care, and services for unaccompanied children referred to ORR but does not describe the entire UC program (e.g., part 411 on prevention of sexual abuse remains in effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will continue to use subregulatory guidance (Policy Guide, Field Guidance, manuals) to clarify application; the NPRM codifies core items while preserving other vehicles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: care provider facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed definition broadly describes any placement type for unaccompanied children (except out of network placements) and is broader than 'standard program'; it encompasses facilities exclusively serving children needing particular services/treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR notes the definition does not reference 'facilities for children with special needs' and intends the term to cover placements where children receive particular services, including those serving special needs children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition distinction: disability vs special needs unaccompanied child
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed definition of 'disability' is distinct from 'special needs unaccompanied child' (the latter derived from FSA); although a child may have both, the terms are not synonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a child may be considered to have a disability under section 504 even if they do not require services/treatment that would make them a 'special needs' child under FSA-derived definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: emergency (context-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed definition of 'emergency' differs from 45 CFR 411.5 and is tailored to the term's usage in the context of requirements in this proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will explain the context-specific meaning where used in the rule (not simply the general sudden/urgent occurrence definition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: EOIR accredited representative terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this proposed rule, ORR adopts the term 'EOIR accredited representative' (DOJ uses 'accredited representative').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a terminology choice for clarity within part 410; it aligns with EOIR/DOJ designations but clarifies naming in the NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: heightened supervision facility (replacing 'staff secure')
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed definition incorporates language consistent with the FSA's 'medium secure facility' and is intended to replace ORR's prior term 'staff secure facility' because that term was not well understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology change aims to better convey the nature of such facilities and reduce confusion about placement types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: influx (updated threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed definition changes the influx threshold (the FSA's 130 minors standard is out of date); the new definition reflects ORR bed capacity and current migration realities so the program is not effectively always in influx status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR developed a more realistic, workable threshold to trigger safeguards when a high percentage of bed capacity is in use; the change is intended to avoid perpetual influx status under the 1997 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: post-release services
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-release services may include assisting with school enrollment, requesting English proficiency assessment, seeking evaluations for special education or accommodations, and monitoring school attendance/progress; TVPRA requires follow-up services during removal proceedings where a home study occurred, subject to resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR clarifies the kinds of assistance that may be provided and notes resource limitations may affect extent of services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition update: 'escape risk' to 'runaway risk'
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes to update 'escape risk' (FSA) to 'runaway risk,' using a totality-of-circumstances approach rather than relying solely on past attempts to abscond; 'runaway risk' is consistent with state child welfare usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will consider runaway risk in placement determinations and interprets 'risk of flight' to include runaway risk, which may overlap with concerns about immigration hearing attendance and danger to self/community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: secure facility (clarified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed definition clarifies secure facility consistent with FSA provisions and differs from the 2019 Final Rule definition to avoid conflating facilities with separate accommodations for minors as inherently secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim is to avoid erroneously characterizing non-secure placements as secure merely because of separate accommodations; definition aligns with placement nature and security features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: special needs unaccompanied child (terminology update)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed definition incorporates FSA 'special needs minor' but updates language to 'intellectual or developmental disability' instead of outdated terms; recognizes overlap but distinction from 'disability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may consider not defining or using 'special needs unaccompanied child' elsewhere in the part, soliciting comment on that approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: standard program (replaces 'licensed program')
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed term 'standard program' updates FSA's 'licensed program' to account for states that discontinue or exempt licensing of facilities that contract with the federal government; 'standard program' is broader and requires meeting minimum standards consistent with FSA Exhibit 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR solicits comment on substituting 'standard program' for 'licensed program' and how to ensure minimum standards where state licensure is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: trauma bond
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed definition of 'trauma bond' is consistent with the Office to Monitor and Combat Trafficking in Persons (DOS) factsheet 'Trauma Bonding in Human Trafficking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation of established trafficking-related terminology to guide assessment and care planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed approach
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR believes a trauma-informed approach to care and placement is essential and understands trauma-informed systems/practices consistent with the CDC/SAMHSA '6 Guidelines To A Trauma-Informed Approach.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes to apply trauma-informed principles across care decisions to ensure children's interests and vulnerabilities are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle: dignity, respect, and special concern (§410.1003(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For all placements, unaccompanied children shall be treated with dignity, respect, and special concern for their particular vulnerability as unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is grounded in statutory duties and the FSA (paragraph 11) and underpins facility and care standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle: safe and sanitary facilities (§410.1003(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall hold unaccompanied children in facilities that are safe and sanitary and consistent with ORR's concern for the particular vulnerability of unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adapts the FSA's paragraph 12A standard (previously applied to arrest/detention) to ORR custody facilities as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized, strengths-based care planning (§410.1003(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must plan and provide care and services based on the individual needs of and focusing on the strengths of the unaccompanied child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes assessment and tailored services rather than one-size-fits-all placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child participation in decision-making (§410.1003(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall, as developmentally appropriate and in the child's best interests, encourage unaccompanied children to be active participants in decisions relating to their care and placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes empowerment, resilience, and self-efficacy through collaborative approaches where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored care and protection from exploitation (§410.1003(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be tailored to individualized needs, ensure the child's interests are considered, and protect unaccompanied children from traffickers and others seeking to victimize or exploit them while in ORR custody and upon release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes assessing whether the child requires services/treatment for issues like severe neglect or abuse (as in FSA paragraph 7) and addressing risks including unscrupulous employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucas R.: step-up class - notice and hearing before secure placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation and class certification that children placed in secure, medium-secure, or residential treatment centers (or detained in such facilities >30 days) were denied notice and opportunity to be heard before a neutral decisionmaker regarding grounds for placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM notes ongoing Lucas R. litigation and that ORR implemented new policies after a preliminary injunction; rulemaking may incorporate provisions responsive to litigated issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucas R.: unfit custodian class - release timeliness and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation and class certification regarding children whom ORR refuses or will refuse to release to parents or custodians within 30 days of a proposed custodian's submission of a complete family reunification packet on grounds the proposed custodian is or may be unfit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects judicial scrutiny over ORR's processes and may inform proposed regulatory language and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucas R.: drug administration class - psychotropic medication safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation and class certification over children prescribed or administered psychotropic medications without procedural safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This highlights the need for procedural protections when psychotropic medications are administered; the NPRM flags potential incorporation of safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucas R.: legal representation class - access for non-contiguous country natives
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation and class certification that ORR impedes legal assistance for natives of non-contiguous countries in matters involving custody, placement, release, and/or administration of psychotropic drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPRM notes litigation and potential regulatory adjustments to ensure access to legal assistance for affected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lucas R.: disability class - placement because of disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegation and class certification regarding children with behavioral, mental health, intellectual, and/or developmental disabilities being placed in secure/medium-secure/RTC because of such disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises concerns about placement decisions and accommodations for children with disabilities; may inform definitions and placement standards in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ninth Circuit limits on HHS regulations from 2019 Final Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ninth Circuit found most HHS regulations 'largely consistent' with the FSA but held two provisions inconsistent: (1) allowing placement in secure facilities upon agency determination that a minor is otherwise a danger to self or others (broadened circumstances), and (2) providing hearings to children in secure/staff-secure placements only if requested (inconsistent with FSA's opt-out bond hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR notes these holdings and that the FSA remains in effect; the NPRM reflects the Ninth Circuit's findings in designing standards that avoid those inconsistencies.
